Definition: from G1722 and G3611; to inhabit (figuratively):--dwell in.
BiblicalUsage: To dwell in — God in us, His word in us, faith in us. God says I will dwell in them in 2 Corinthians 6:16, the word of Christ is to dwell in us richly in Colossians 3:16, and the Spirit who raised Jesus dwells in us in Romans 8:11. Timothy's unfeigned faith dwelt first in his grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice in 2 Timothy 1:5.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe dwelling is God's way — He does not visit and leave, He moves in, and His word and His Spirit take up residence in me. I hold that a faith that dwelt in a grandmother and a mother can dwell in a grandson too, and that is how the gospel travels: from one home to the next.
RelatedTopics: Presence of God; Word of God; Outpouring of the Spirit
